lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

Federal Kayfabe: the money in your wallet is somebody's debt, and you are the collateral.

Kayfabe, for the newcomers, is wrestling slang for a staged fight sold as real.

Tonight we read the terms and conditions on your money, one card at a time.

Print a twenty in your basement, that's prison. A banker types a million into a laptop, that's a loan.

History nerds, you know the trip: Senator Aldrich's private rail car, bound for Jekyll Island.

Uncle FrizzleBob's Federal Reserve Secret: debt slavery disguised as stability; watch it burn.

The Creature from the Fed: not Federal, no Reserve; a cartel bought the right to print money.

Print rights? Presto. Fiat Conjuring: money typed into existence, backed by your grandparents’ promises.

Economic Jargon: of all the sciences, monetary complexity is chosen for the fraud; Galbraith.

In English: a lion. Bank of England: King William's war debts, and a private bank wearing a state mask.

Fractional Reserve Illusion: only five percent ask for gold; the power was belief.

Bank of North America: missing founding, first private U.S. bank; war funding before freedom.

War's over, debt stays. Alexander Hamilton's Ghost: if debt exists, let the elite own it; history agreed.

First Bank of the U.S.: Hamilton’s pet project loaned the government, made the bankers rich.

Thomas Jefferson's Warning: banking, more dangerous to our liberties than standing armies.

Warning ignored. Second Bank of the U.S.: another monopoly over money that hurt the working class.

Andrew Jackson Kills a Bank: killed the bank, and all I got was this weird election and a duel.

No bank? Grab a board. The Gilded Oligarchs: competition was cute; next stop, governing the money itself.

Conductor? A clown. Pierpont Morgan: he was the market; king of the Panic becomes king of the rescue.

The Panic of Nineteen Oh Seven: the public begged for a solution; the bankers provided one.

Drafted in advance. The Aldrich Plan: private meeting; the public has to believe this was their idea.

Jekyll Island Duck Hunt: secret, fake names; what if private bankers wrote public banking law?

Nelson Aldrich: Rockefeller’s father-in-law, legislative inside man on the train of old money.

Old money's spider. Paul Warburg: if I know central banking and you don’t, trust me, I’m saving you.

Frank Vanderlip's Confession: I was as furtive as any conspirator; Jekyll Island happened.

Into the Capitol. The Trojan Horse Act: sold as decentralization; a cartel in patriotic wrapping paper.

Woodrow Wilson's Pen: most unhappy man; I unwittingly ruined my country by a system of credit.

Pen out, snow falling. The Christmas Eve Smuggling: Congress was home; timing, the midnight superpower.

Who runs the coop? The Fox in the Henhouse: bankers design their regulator and call it a federal agency.

Book Money: over ninety percent isn’t printed; it’s typed into existence as a loan by banks.

Loan signed? Run. The Interest Trap: principal is created, interest is not; guaranteed bankruptcies.

Purchasing Power Theft: inflation is a hidden tax, created by expanding the money supply.

Not hidden: an anvil. The Taxpayer Backstop: bankers gamble and lose, and the taxpayer is the collateral.

Basement printer: twenty years. The Fed's printer since nineteen thirteen: prices up thirty times, and we call that price stability.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!
lyrics2:
[Spoken Word]

Federal Kayfabe, part two: the Fed breaks the economy, says sorry, and the public pays the bill.

I'm your narrator tonight: thirty-two satire cards, read over a beat, one breath each.

Overdraw five bucks and the bank fines you thirty-five. Banks crash the whole country, and you pay their fine.

For insiders: gold booked at forty-two twenty-two an ounce, a General Counsel named Alvarez, and Carroll Quigley.

The Roaring Twenties Bubble: the Fed pumped the money supply; a drunken decade on cheap credit.

But the dance ended. The Great Depression: the Fed contracted the money supply; a decade of mass poverty.

Milton Friedman's Diagnosis: economists admitted the Fed created and exacerbated the panic.

So the fish shrugs. Bernanke's Hollow Apology: you’re right, we did it. Very sorry. We won’t do it again.

The Nineteen Thirty-Four Gold Heist: the government seized the people's gold; wealth for paper.

In return, a note. Gold Certificates: Treasury bookkeeping ghosts representing assets they don't possess.

Ask the snake. Scott Alvarez's Denial: no gold at all; the General Counsel admits the emperor is naked.

The Four-Twenty-Two Dollar Arbitrary Peg: phantom gold valued by law; bookkeeping sorcery.

Board of Governors: public face; they answer to no one and laugh at Congressional funding.

Who owns it? The Regional Reserve Banks: privately owned; public central bank, private dividend machine.

The New York Fed: for Wall Street banks it exerts final dominance; zero public accountability.

The F.O.M.C.: private bankers set interest rates, steering the economy for their portfolios.

The Two Thousand Eight Subprime Crash: casino collapsed; the public never leaves the table.

Refill the casino. Quantitative Easing: money creation straight to the top; everyone else gets inflation.

The Ouroboros Rescue: banks buy bonds with bailout money and charge the taxpayer interest.

Rescued, the hippo. Too Big to Fail: lose? Please. I’m too important; if I fall, the economy gets blamed.

Council on Foreign Relations: Morgan allies place bankers, politicians in a single hive-mind.

Bank for International Settlements: the central bank of central banks in Basel, above the law.

The Feudal Endgame: worldwide financial control of each political system, says Carroll Quigley.

Global Governance: they say engineered crashes are justification for planetary economic power.

The Audit Movement: Ron Paul's grassroots; the Fed fought sunlight like vampires fight mirrors.

End the Fed Protests: Boston to Wall Street; once peasants learn accounting, empires sweat.

Bank of North Dakota: a state-owned bank that outperforms the Wall Street casino regularly.

Ellen Brown: public banks redirect deposits; public banking cuts parasites, not funding.

Ithaca Hours: local currency backed by human labor; actual neighbors trade for actual potatoes.

Beyond potatoes. The Time-Barter Rogue: armed with graphic design and arrogance, he made mutual credit.

Bitcoin: decentralized network, no central server, no CEO; mathematics over manipulation.

So trust no printer. The Un-Printable Math: if you trust money to stay power, you trust it to your enemy.

Cut the strings. The Paradigm Shift: system collapses under disbelief; the illusion requires your belief.

The Counter-Economy: alternative networks, sound money; quietly starve the beast of compliance.

The Century of Empowerment: feudal debt slavery, or trade and human empowerment; a choice.

So, scissors out. Kayfabizarro Anarchy: hand the myth to people, epistemic sabotage, and burn the ledger.

Next time you overdraw five bucks, ask your bank for the Bernanke deal: one sorry, zero consequences.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!
